text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they regularly add it to a shared project. This triggers automated builds, which means the system compiles the code without anyone doing it by hand. As part of the process, the CI pipeline also runs tests automatically. These tests check whether the new code works correctly and doesn't break anything else. The main benefit is catching issues early, before they become big problems. If something fails, the team knows immediately and can fix it quickly. This keeps the software stable and helps developers work together more easily.
